kind: Fintech Launch Strategy · The Tirano Pay story, part 2
title: Tirano Pay
subtitle: A Swiss fintech, planned from the name to Germany
note: Tirano Pay is an example name for an example company: payments and cash-flow software for Swiss small and mid-sized companies, Switzerland first, then Germany. Part 1 found the name; this part plans the company. Every finding is an Antevo engine's answer on the date shown, or an official page read that day; where an engine named a company, the page describes it instead. The plan, the gates and the measures are the assistant's options to consider, not advice.

thesis.label: The strategy in one paragraph
thesis.text: Launch in Switzerland first as software that holds no client money: it reads a company's bank accounts, forecasts its cash and prepares payments the bank executes. That reaches paying customers without waiting for a licence. Ask FINMA early, in a preliminary assessment, whether that first product needs one. Apply for the licence second, built to fit both the FinTech licence and the new category the Federal Council proposed. Enter Germany third, under a licensed EU partner before an EU licence of its own, because a Swiss licence does not reach the EU. Earn from fees, not from client balances: at a zero policy rate there is no float income, and the FinTech licence forbids paying interest anyway. Raise early, while the window is open, and let each stage start only when its gate is passed.

items.name: The name

No Swiss company under the name
tiranopay.ch and tiranopay.com appear unregistered

items.name: The field
evidence: A search of the Swiss register for payments companies fills its first page
They cluster in central Switzerland: Zug, Rotkreuz, Immensee and Küssnacht among them, with others in Zurich, Bern and Vaud
The fintech search shows the same pull: five of the first ten sit in Zug or Baar

items.name: The licence
evidence: The FinTech licence lets a company take public deposits up to CHF 100 million, if they are not invested and no interest is paid
A business subject to the Anti-Money Laundering Act must join a self-regulatory organisation; FINMA lists payment transactions among those likely to be
FINMA offers a fast track for low-risk business models after a successful preliminary assessment, case by case
On 22 October 2025 the Federal Council proposed payment instrument institutions, to replace the FinTech licence and lift the CHF 100 million limit; no dispatch to Parliament was found

items.name: Germany
evidence: German business sentiment rose again in November; manufacturing and composite surveys stood at 55, the fastest activity in over four years
Switzerland is not in the EU's single market for financial services: a Swiss licence cannot be passported
To hold or move German companies' money, a firm needs an EU licence, from BaFin or from another EU state and passported

items.name: Money and timing
evidence: The newest large AI listing fell below its offer price on 24 November; the response the radar lists is to lock in funding early
The economy desk reads venture funding as tighter, after the largest rotation out of tech in two decades
The Swiss National Bank's rate is 0.00%; it decides next on 10 December
Markets are elevated, 2.42 times a normal week, easing from 3.84

plan.label: Twelve months, four stages, each with a gate

items.title: Foundation
do: File Tirano Pay in Switzerland in classes 9, 36 and 42, then watch it
Register the company and both domains
Ask FINMA for a preliminary assessment of the first product and of the licence route
Choose the anti-money-laundering self-regulatory organisation, if the assessment says the law applies
Open the funding round while the window is open
items.gate: FINMA's preliminary view is in hand, the name is filed, and the round has a lead investor

items.title: Launch without holding money
do: Release cash forecasting and payment preparation to the first Swiss companies, through their own banks
Connect more than one bank from the start, so no single bank's access decides the product
Price by subscription and fee, never by balances held
items.gate: Pilot companies are paying and renewing, and the measures below have the thresholds set at the first gate

items.title: The licence
do: File the licence application on FINMA's platform, under the fast track if the preliminary assessment allows it
Write the application so it maps to both the FinTech licence and a payment instrument institution
Build the anti-money-laundering and data controls to Swiss and EU standards at once
items.gate: The application is filed with no fundamental concerns raised, and the runway reaches past the licence decision

items.title: Germany
do: Choose the route: a licensed EU partner first, or an EU licence of Tirano Pay's own
Read the EU payment rules as published, and build to them
Run the first German pilot with companies selling into German industry
items.gate: The EU payment rules are final, a partner or a licence covers German clients' money, and the first German companies are live

risks.label: Risks, each with the sign that would set it off

items.trigger: A large AI-linked sale prices wide of guidance or is pulled; Tremor Watch reads high again with credit breaking
items.response: Close the round on the terms available and stretch the runway; move Germany back a stage

items.trigger: The Federal Council sends the payment instrument institutions bill to Parliament
items.response: Keep the application mapped to both regimes, so a switch is an update, not a restart

items.trigger: A partner bank withdraws or reprices its access; in Switzerland that access rests on contracts, not on a legal right
items.response: Several banks from launch; no stage depends on one

items.trigger: The euro falls further against the franc; it was 0.9163 francs on 25 November, down 1.6% on the year
items.response: Price Germany in euros with a review clause, and keep costs in the currency the revenue comes in

items.risk: EU rules arrive late or different
items.trigger: The European Parliament's vote on the payment rules, set for around 14 December, slips or reopens the text
items.response: Hold the German build at the partner route until the text is final

items.trigger: A new mark close to Tirano Pay is filed
items.response: Antevo Trademark watch on the name; a lawyer reviews any close filing

sections.title: Rates and the franc
sections.so_what: With the policy rate at zero and interest banned under the FinTech licence, every franc of revenue has to come from fees: build the price list before the product, not after.
evidence: The Swiss National Bank's rate is 0.00% and Swiss inflation 1.5%; the desk expects rises from spring 2027
EUR/CHF 0.9163, down 1.6% on the year
The European Central Bank's rate is 2.50%

sections.title: EU rules in motion
sections.so_what: The German product should be built to the new EU payment rules from the start: they will govern it from about late 2027 or early 2028.
evidence: The Council of the EU adopted its positions on the new payment services rules on 29 October; the Parliament's vote is indicated for around 14 December
Instant euro payments are already required of EU payment providers: a baseline, not a feature
The EU's new anti-money-laundering rulebook applies in 2027; its authority supervises selected firms directly from 2028

sections.title: Swiss developments
sections.so_what: Neither changes the first year; both could change the product in the second, so the plan keeps them on the watchlist.
evidence: The Swiss National Bank and SIX launched an exploration of a Swiss Financial Ledger on 24 November
The proposed payment instrument institutions would replace the FinTech licence; consultation ran to 6 February 2026

items.do: Register the company and the domains
items.why: No Swiss company uses the name and both domains appear free; either can change at any time.
It answers the first question of the plan, whether the first product needs a licence, and it is the condition for the fast track.

The application should fit the law that may replace the FinTech licence.
An EU licence from BaFin or another EU state, or a licensed EU partner first.

links.text: The name is clear, and the register shows a crowded field: Tirano Pay stands apart by the problem it solves for small companies, not by being one more payments firm.
Zero rates remove float income and the funding window is narrowing: both point to a fee-based product that reaches paying customers before the licence.
German demand is the strongest in four years, and a Swiss licence does not reach it: the opportunity sets the fourth stage, the rules set its route.
Elevated but easing markets and a dated calendar argue for opening the round now and closing it on a calm week, not on a headline.
